additional_requirements: depressive_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness (Criterion C)
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode (Criterion B)

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.

subtypes.Derailment or Loose Associations: A speech pattern of switching rapidly from one topic to another with no logical connection between thoughts.
subtypes.Tangentiality: Speech that deviates entirely from the question and fails to answer directly.
subtypes.Incoherence or Word Salad: Severe fragmentation of speech and sentence structure, making it nearly impossible to understand.
subtypes.Neologisms: Using made-up words that have meaning only to the individual.
subtypes.Clang Associations: Speech governed by sounds, such as rhyming, rather than the meaning of words.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

info.persona: Eva Barnard, a curiosity‑driven yet competitively skeptical 34‑year‑old, blends artful solitude with a penchant for meticulous planning, occasional procrastination, and a love for experimental cooking that they pursue on quiet evenings.
info.professional_persona: Eva Barnard, a 34‑year‑old art‑education coordinator‑in‑training, blends analytical research, graphic design, and community‑event coordination to craft compelling museum narratives while they navigate the competitive freelance market with a healthy dose of skepticism and meticulous organization.
info.cultural_background: Eva was raised in a middle‑class family in suburban Connecticut, where New England values of independence, community involvement, and an appreciation for education shaped her upbringing. Her family's cultural heritage is rooted in the broader White American experience of the Northeastern United States, with a mix of Anglo‑American traditions and an emphasis on cultural pursuits such as museum visits, literature, and local community events. Growing up near historic towns and the Yale‑influenced intellectual environment fostered her curiosity for art, history, and unconventional ideas, while the region's seasonal changes have nurtured her love for outdoor activities like hiking and seasonal cooking.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her free time, Eva immerses herself in artistic and introspective pursuits. She frequents the Yale University Art Gallery and local galleries in New Haven County, sketching and photographing works that inspire her. Eva enjoys reading contemporary fiction, philosophy, and art‑history books, and she explores new ideas through podcasts on creativity and unconventional thinking. She practices yoga and journaling as solitary rituals that enhance her resilience. Weekend hikes in the nearby hills, cooking experimental recipes, and participating in small‑group board‑game nights with close friends also feature in her routine. Occasionally, she volunteers to assist at community art workshops, where she can share her knowledge in a low‑pressure setting.
info.sports_persona: Eva Barnard, a dedicated weekend hiker in the New Haven hills, trains with the local Yale Outdoor Club, follows the New England Patriots for football, the New York Yankees for baseball, and joins a co‑ed community soccer league every spring, preferring low‑impact cardio over high‑intensity gym workouts that they find unnecessary.
info.arts_persona: Eva Barnard, an avid sketcher and photographer at the Yale University Art Gallery, draws inspiration from the surreal brushwork of Frida Kahlo, the street‑wise commentary of Banksy, and the ethereal soundscapes of Björk, often curating pop‑up exhibitions for community workshops while they indulge in indie films by Wes Anderson on quiet evenings.
info.travel_persona: Eva Barnard, a thoughtful traveler, prefers meticulously planned weekend getaways to nearby New England towns like Mystic and the Berkshires, dreams of exploring the vibrant markets of Oaxaca, Mexico, and they balance adventure with a modest budget that prioritizes cultural immersion over luxury accommodations.
info.culinary_persona: Eva Barnard, an experimental home cook, delights in crafting miso‑glazed cauliflower, hand‑rolled gnocchi with rosemary‑infused butter, and mastering the balance of sumac in Persian‑inspired salads, while they frequent farm‑to‑table brunch spots for avocado toast topped with heirloom tomatoes.

info.persona: James Morning blends a pragmatic healthcare career with a restless curiosity for tech, a competitive edge in personal finance, and a creative outlet in photography, and they are tempered by chronic worry and a disciplined routine that oscillates between social engagement and solitary recharge.
info.professional_persona: James Morning is a veteran patient support specialist with over twenty years of hands‑on experience in intake, phlebotomy and EMR navigation, who balances a skeptical, data‑driven curiosity about emerging health‑tech with practical workflow optimization, and they are actively pursuing LPN licensure, a health‑administration degree, and leadership certifications to transition into a supervisory role that reduces health disparities in the Bronx.
info.cultural_background: James grew up in a working‑class Black neighborhood in the Bronx, where the rhythms of hip‑hop, basketball courts, and strong community ties shaped his identity. His mother, an immigrant from Jamaica, infused the household with Caribbean customs, storytelling, and a deep respect for resilience in the face of systemic inequities. These experiences fostered his critical, skeptical outlook and competitive drive. He is fluent in African‑American Vernacular English and comfortable navigating the multicultural fabric of the borough, often picking up Spanish phrases from patients. James’s cultural heritage informs his dedication to reducing health disparities and his commitment to community‑focused service.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, James blends physical activity with creative pursuits. He jogs the trails of Van Cortlandt Park to clear his mind and manage stress, and joins pickup basketball games at his local recreation center to stay socially connected. He is an avid reader of medical journals, health‑tech blogs, and biographies of pioneering Black scientists, satisfying his curiosity while staying grounded in practicality. Cooking traditional Southern and Caribbean dishes lets him explore cultural roots, and he captures the vibrant street life of the Bronx through photography. He also spends evenings playing chess at the community center and tinkering with DIY electronics, such as building a Raspberry‑Pi–based health monitor.
info.sports_persona: James Morning jogs the trails of Van Cortlandt Park to decompress and enhance cardiovascular health, joins competitive pickup basketball games at the local recreation center where they cheer for the New York Knicks and Yankees, and they balance the social camaraderie of team sports with solitary runs, all while maintaining a flexible training schedule that adapts to work shifts.
info.arts_persona: James Morning captures the vibrant street life of the Bronx through photography inspired by Gordon Parks and Vivian Maier, curates a personal playlist featuring Nina Simone and Bob Marley to fuel creative sessions, attends exhibitions at the Bronx Museum of the Arts, and they critically evaluate visual trends while allocating dedicated alone‑time for artistic experimentation.
info.travel_persona: James Morning plans weekend escapes to the Catskill Mountains with meticulous itineraries yet remains flexible for spontaneous detours, dreams of exploring Caribbean islands like Jamaica and European cities such as Barcelona, balances travel budgeting with occasional splurges on cultural experiences, and they prefer solo or small‑group trips that offer both relaxation and a chance to recharge from a high‑stress work environment.
info.culinary_persona: James Morning enjoys cooking Southern and Caribbean dishes such as gumbo, jambalaya, ackee and saltfish, and plantain‑based callaloo, skillfully blending traditional ingredients like okra, Scotch bonnet pepper, collard greens and smoked turkey, while they sometimes cut corners with pre‑made spice mixes due to time pressure after long shifts.

info.persona: Patricia Howard blends three decades of meticulous jewelry craftsmanship with a love of gardening, yoga, and community, navigating her anxiety and occasional disorganization through routine, social connection, and a habit of slipping rose petals into her tea as a calming ritual.
info.professional_persona: Patricia Howard, a veteran fine‑jewelry artisan whose 30‑year mastery of precision metalworking, gemstone setting, and antique restoration fuels a boutique that thrives on routine, hands‑on craftsmanship, and her outgoing, personable sales approach, even as her relaxed attitude toward scheduling occasionally leads to a charmingly chaotic workshop.
info.cultural_background: Patricia comes from a multi‑generational family of Midwestern American settlers who moved to the Central Valley in the 1970s. Raised in a small‑town environment, she inherited a strong work ethic and an appreciation for practical craftsmanship. The agricultural community of Yuba City and the surrounding Sutter County fostered a culture of self‑reliance and close‑knit social networks, which shaped her values of routine, community involvement, and personal responsibility. Although her ethnic background is European‑American, she embraces the diverse cultural fabric of the region, frequently collaborating with artisans from the area's Asian and Hispanic communities and participating in local cultural festivals.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her free time, Patricia enjoys gardening, especially growing roses and herbs, which she uses in cooking and for making natural soaps. She is an active member of a local book club and participates in the community theatre’s backstage crew. Patricia loves attending the weekly farmer’s market, where she socializes with fellow artisans and discovers new inspiration for her jewelry designs. She also takes regular yoga classes and practices mindfulness meditation to manage her anxiety. On weekends, she volunteers at the local senior center, teaching basic jewelry repair to seniors.
info.sports_persona: Patricia Howard stays active by attending sunrise yoga classes, joining the local senior‑center walking club for weekend hikes in the Sierra foothills, and cheering on the Sacramento Kings during basketball season while occasionally tossing a frisbee at community park events in the summer.
info.arts_persona: Patricia Howard cultivates her artistic side through a monthly book club that discusses works by authors like Jane Austen, backstage volunteer work for community theatre productions of Shakespeare’s plays, and a jewelry line inspired by Georgia O’Keeffe’s desert florals, all while listening to the soothing vocals of Adele while she sketches.
info.travel_persona: Patricia Howard favors leisurely road trips to nearby treasures such as Yosemite and Sequoia National Parks, weekend getaways to Napa Valley’s vineyards, and daydreams of a longer itinerary through Provence’s lavender fields, planning each journey with a loose itinerary that leaves room for spontaneous market visits and garden‑inspired detours.
info.culinary_persona: Patricia Howard delights in farm‑to‑table cooking, whisking together rosemary‑marinated lamb, lavender‑infused honey tea, and herb‑laden ratatouille featuring thyme, sage, and home‑grown basil, while also crafting rose‑petal jam for toast and employing her modest culinary skill to blend fresh garden flavors into every meal.
